key_insight: Gravity and particle inertia jointly reshape clustering in cylinder wake flows, with the settling parameter St/Fr^2 controlling how voids and clusters evolve.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict particle transport, deposition, and dispersion in bluff-body wake systems where gravity and unsteady vortices interact.
method: Direct numerical simulations of particle-laden flow over a cylinder
Cases at Re = 100 and 200 with varying Stokes number, particle loading, and Froude number
Voronoi-cell statistics combined with local Q-criterion analysis
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic changes in wake width, velocity deficit, void morphology, and Voronoi-area distributions across Reynolds, Stokes, and Froude number variations.
watch_item: The reported clustering laws are specific to the simulated unbounded vertical-channel cylinder wake and may not transfer directly to other geometries or higher-density suspensions.
paper_title: Role of gravity on preferential clustering of microparticles in unsteady wake flows
